comment: SYNTHETIC MITRE ATT&CK lookup table for the forensics-agent evaluation scenarios (ransom01, lateral01, exfil01). Committed by tools-engineer as static data for the lookup_mitre_technique tool. Technique IDs/names/tactics summarize the public MITRE ATT&CK knowledge base; descriptions are short paraphrases written for this project. Unknown IDs are NEVER guessed: the tool returns found=false instead.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.description: Adversaries attempt to dump credentials to obtain account logon and session material, commonly via LSASS memory, registry hives, or credential stores.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
techniques.description: Adversaries attempt to access credential material stored in the process memory of the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS), e.g. via comsvcs MiniDump or Mimikatz.

techniques.name: Remote Services
techniques.description: Adversaries use valid accounts to interact with remote services such as RDP, SMB/admin shares, or WinRM to move laterally between hosts.

techniques.name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries use valid accounts to interact with a remote host using the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), often for interactive lateral movement.

techniques.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: Adversaries use SMB/Windows Admin Shares to access remote hosts' file systems and transfer tools or payloads during lateral movement.

techniques.name: Remote Services: Windows Remote Management
techniques.description: Adversaries use WinRM to run commands on a remote host over HTTP(S), often via Invoke-Command or winrs.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.description: Adversaries steal data by sending it over the same command-and-control channel used for control of the compromised host.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries steal data by transferring it over a non-standard protocol or port (e.g. DNS, ICMP, or an uncommon TCP service) to avoid detection.

techniques.name: Process Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries inject code into running processes to evade process-based defenses and gain elevated access.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Adversaries execute commands and scripts via interpreters such as Unix shells, PowerShell, or Windows Command Shell.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries use PowerShell to execute commands and payloads, often encoded or obfuscated, to download or run malicious code.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries use cmd.exe to execute commands and scripts, e.g. to run ransomware preparation steps such as deleting volume shadow copies.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
techniques.description: Adversaries clear Windows Event Logs (e.g. via wevtutil cl) to erase evidence of their activity.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
techniques.description: Adversaries communicate over web protocols such as HTTP/S for command-and-control, blending in with normal browsing traffic.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries use credentials of existing accounts (default, compromised, or local admin) to gain initial access, persistence, or privilege escalation.

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate files and directories (e.g. recursive listings before encryption or exfiltration) to locate data of interest.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate local and domain accounts to identify targets for lateral movement and privilege escalation.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries transfer tools or additional payloads from an external system to the compromised host, e.g. over the C2 channel.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.description: Adversaries attempt to guess passwords, passphrases, or keys via repeated authentication attempts (password spraying, credential stuffing).

techniques.name: User Execution: Malicious File
techniques.description: Adversaries rely on a user opening a malicious file (e.g. a macro-laced document or attached executable) to gain execution.

techniques.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
techniques.description: Adversaries exploit vulnerabilities in remote services (e.g. SMB, RDP) to move laterally to other hosts in the network.

techniques.name: Data Destruction
techniques.description: Adversaries destroy data and files on systems to disrupt availability or cover tracks, e.g. overwriting or deleting business-critical files.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.description: Adversaries encrypt data on target systems to disrupt availability (ransomware) and demand payment for decryption.

techniques.name: Service Stop
techniques.description: Adversaries stop or disable services (e.g. backup, database, or security services) to aid destruction or evade defenses.

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.description: Adversaries delete volume shadow copies, backups, or recovery partitions to prevent the victim from restoring encrypted data.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.description: Adversaries disable or modify security tools (antivirus, EDR, logging) to avoid detection of their activity.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: Adversaries send targeted emails with malicious attachments (e.g. macro documents, archives) to gain initial access.

techniques.name: Encrypted Channel
techniques.description: Adversaries use an encrypted protocol (e.g. HTTPS with a symmetric cipher) to hide command-and-control traffic.
